card: This PR adds an AssertUnreachable() macro to util/check.h and mechanically replaces assert(false) and Assert(false) patterns across the codebase, backed by a new linter. It eliminates -Wreturn-type warnings across GCC and clang-cl while avoiding the undefined behavior risk of C++23 std::unreachable. Importance is evidenced by compiler warning reproducers across supported toolchains. It has no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Added a commit removing unused includes from src/test/util_tests.cpp as requested in review.
evidence: PR description links to a Compiler Explorer reproducer demonstrating -Wreturn-type warnings on GCC and clang-cl with the previous assertions: https://godbolt.org/z/h7PT3jh3Y
problem: Using assert(false) causes compiler warnings under clang-cl and raises ambiguity over whether NDEBUG disables the check, while Assert(false) obscures the noreturn attribute and triggers -Wreturn-type warnings under GCC. Additionally, developers adopting C++23 patterns might use std::unreachable(), which invokes undefined behavior rather than cleanly aborting.

risk.why: A mistake in the macro or mechanical replacement could cause unintended aborts or failure to abort on unreachable branches, but the macro directly maps to the existing abort helper.

scope_notes: The vast majority of the change is mechanical: a scripted diff replacing falsy assertions across ~80 files, accompanied by include adjustments and a new linter check in test/lint/test_runner/.
summary: Introduces an AssertUnreachable() macro in util/check.h that directly calls internal_abort_helper with [[noreturn]] semantics. Mechanically replaces assert(false), Assert(false), and equivalent unreachable aborts across the codebase via scripted diff, eliminates dead return code, and introduces a Rust-based assert_falsy linter to enforce its use.
